mainTopic: The mixed-up tenth and eleventh animal in מעשר בהמה, and an agent who mislabels the tithe animal
overview: The גמרא resolves two ברייתות about a mixed-up tenth and eleventh animal in מעשר בהמה. The 'sacrifice both' ruling follows רבי שמעון, who allows bringing קדשים into a situation where they might become disqualified. The 'both die' ruling is first assigned to רבי יהודה, who calls a mistaken מעשר a תמורה. Our משנה, a ברייתא and an unattributed ספרא all show that רבי יהודה holds the eleventh animal is offered as a שלמים, so that assignment fails. Instead, רבי שמעון ברבי אבא explains that the 'both die' ברייתא is about מעשר nowadays: the animals cannot be offered, so they are left to die out of concern for a תקלה, even when two animals mean a bigger loss. Next, רב פפי and רב פפא disagree about an agent who calls the ninth animal 'tenth'. רב פפא says it is not holy, because the owner sent him to help, not to harm. The גמרא distinguishes this from an agent who gives more or less תרומה, which is a reasonable estimate and not a mistake. The amud closes with the הדרן for פרק מעשר בהמה and the completion of מסכת בכורות.

steps.title: The ruling 'sacrifice both' follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says both mixed-up animals are sacrificed follows רבי שמעון. He holds that one may bring קדשים into a situation where they risk becoming disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that teaches 'they should be sacrificed' follows רבי שמעון. He says one may bring holy animals into a situation that risks disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reconciling two ברייתות that disagree, and here it assigns the first one ('sacrifice both') to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a מעשר animal and a שלמים animal are mixed, you must follow the stricter rules of both. That limits how the meat can be handled and creates more chances that the meat becomes disqualified. רבי שמעון permits this anyway, so for him both animals can be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: One may bring holy offerings into a situation where they may become disqualified

phrases.english: And this one who teaches: 'they shall be sacrificed' —
it is Rabbi Shimon, who says:
one may bring sacred animals to a situation of disqualification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the two ברייתות that was raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא follows רבי שמעון's leniency of מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול.

steps.title: The ruling 'both must die' follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says both animals must die follows רבי יהודה. He holds that a mistaken מעשר has the status of a תמורה, and that a תמורת מעשר is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that teaches 'they should die' follows רבי יהודה. He says a mistake in מעשר counts as a תמורה, and רבי יהודה holds that a תמורת מעשר is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assigns the second ברייתא ('both die') to רבי יהודה and explains his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the eleventh animal mistakenly called 'tenth' is a תמורה of the מעשר. A תמורת מעשר cannot be offered and must die. Since we do not know which animal is the eleventh, both are left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: They should be left to die
A mistake in designating the tenth animal
A substitute animal that receives holiness from an existing קרבן
A substitute of a tithe animal is left to die

steps.confusionAlert: 'Left to die' does not mean someone kills the animal. It is locked in a pen without food until it dies, because it cannot be offered or redeemed.

phrases.english: And this one who teaches: 'they shall die' —
it is Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
a mistake in tithe is a substitute,
for Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the substitute of a tithe animal dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the resolution by assigning the second ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to give conflicting rulings in the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ברייתא follows רבי יהודה: the mistaken animal is a תמורה, and a תמורת מעשר dies.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה implies רבי יהודה holds the eleventh is sacrificed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really holds that a תמורת מעשר dies. In the משנה, רבי מאיר answered him: 'If it were a תמורה, it would not be offered.' That implies רבי יהודה held it is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that a תמורת מעשר dies? But we learned in the משנה: they said in the name of רבי מאיר, 'If it were a תמורה, it would not be offered.' This implies that רבי יהודה holds it is offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation of רבי יהודה given in step 2, using the wording of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reply only makes sense as an argument against רבי יהודה if רבי יהודה agreed the eleventh animal is offered. So for רבי יהודה, the eleventh is offered even though it is a תמורה. That contradicts the claim that he holds it dies.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold
that the substitute of a tithe animal dies?
But didn't we learn: they said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
if it were a substitute,
it would not be offered;
by implication, Rabbi Yehuda holds it is offered!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה תְּמוּרַת מַעֲשֵׂר מֵתָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given for רבי יהודה in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds תמורת מעשר מתה in this case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's argument against רבי יהודה assumes that רבי יהודה agrees the eleventh animal is offered.

steps.title: Suggested deflection: רבי מאיר spoke from his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible way out. Maybe רבי מאיר was speaking from his own opinion, so his words prove nothing about רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי מאיר spoke according to what he himself holds...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the challenge, but only to set it up for rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבי מאיר holds the eleventh is offered, so he argued that it cannot be a תמורה. רבי יהודה, though, might hold that it is a תמורה and therefore dies. If so, nothing can be learned about רבי יהודה from רבי מאיר's words.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a proposed answer, usually about to be rejected)
According to what he himself holds

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמַאי דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir was speaking according to what he himself holds,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמַאי דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A suggested defense against the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the inference to the speaker's own view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's words show what רבי יהודה holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's words reflect only his own view and prove nothing about רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה himself holds the eleventh is offered
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying the only difference between the eleventh animal and a שלמים concerns the holiness of a substitute. That implies the eleventh itself is offered, so the deflection fails and the challenge stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'The only difference between the eleventh animal and a שלמים is this. The שלמים makes its substitute holy enough to be offered, and the eleventh does not make its substitute holy enough to be offered. These are the words of רבי יהודה.' So the only thing the eleventh cannot do is make a substitute that is offered. The eleventh animal itself, though, is offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the deflection from step 4 by quoting רבי יהודה directly, which brings the challenge from step 3 back in full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lists only one difference between the eleventh animal and a שלמים: whether its own substitute can be offered. If the eleventh itself had to die, that would be a much bigger difference, and he would have mentioned it. So in רבי יהודה's own words, the eleventh is offered, which contradicts step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives its substitute holiness strong enough to be offered

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge stands: רבי יהודה calls the eleventh a תמורה, yet his own words show it is offered. So how can the 'both die' ברייתא follow him? Steps 6-7 add more proof, and Step 8 gives a new explanation of that ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the eleventh animal with ITS substitute. The ברייתא says the eleventh's substitute cannot be offered. It does not say that about the eleventh animal itself.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
there is no difference between the eleventh and a peace offering,
except that this one makes sanctity to be offered,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the שלמים: its substitute can be offered.

phrases.english: and that one does not make sanctity to be offered,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: קָדוֹשׁ לִיקְרַב הוּא דְּלָא הוּא עָבֵיד,
phrases.english: It is only 'sanctified to be offered' that it does not make,
but it itself is offered!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין אַחַד עָשָׂר לִשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the deflection of step 4 and brings back the challenge of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי מאיר's words do not reflect רבי יהודה's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's own words in a ברייתא show that the eleventh animal is offered, so there is no need to rely on רבי מאיר's words.

steps.title: A second proof from the ספרא that the eleventh animal is offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא: the פסוק 'אם מן הבקר' includes the eleventh animal as a שלמים. It also explains why the ninth animal is not included: a substitute only becomes holy after the real tenth was sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is more proof, because a ברייתא teaches: 'If of the herd' comes to include the eleventh animal as a שלמים. You might think I should also include the ninth. You can answer: does consecration make a substitute holy before the original, or after it? You must say it only works after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another proof that the eleventh animal is offered on the מזבח. This strengthens the challenge from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אם מן הבקר' teaches that the eleventh animal, called 'tenth' by mistake, is brought as a שלמים. The ninth animal is different, because it came before the real tenth. The rule is that a mistaken name can only carry holiness over after the original animal was made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which brings an additional proof
To include, meaning the פסוק adds something extra
The eleventh animal, which was called 'tenth' by mistake
The ninth animal, which was called 'tenth' by mistake
Consecration, the act of making something holy

steps.confusionAlert: The ninth animal does not lose all holiness. It is still holy, just not as a שלמים. Elsewhere it is eaten once it gets a blemish. The ברייתא only says the ninth is not included as a שלמים.

phrases.english: And furthermore, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"If [he sacrifice] of the herd"
phrases.notes: ויקרא ג:א, which is about a שלמים

phrases.english: comes to include the eleventh animal as a peace offering.
One might think that I include even the ninth?
You can say: Does consecration sanctify what comes before it
or does it sanctify what comes after it?
You must say it sanctifies what comes after it.
phrases.notes: So only the eleventh, which comes after the real tenth, becomes a שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source next to the ברייתא of Step 5, both showing that the eleventh animal is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That the eleventh animal mistakenly called מעשר is brought as a שלמים, not left to die.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in the ספרא learning from 'אם מן הבקר'.

steps.title: The ספרא follows רבי יהודה, so he holds the eleventh is offered
steps.stepSummary: An unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה. So it is רבי יהודה himself who teaches that the eleventh animal is offered as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is an unattributed ספרא? רבי יהודה. And it teaches: 'of the herd' comes to include the eleventh animal as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by identifying the author of the ספרא as רבי יהודה. This means רבי יהודה cannot hold that the eleventh animal dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that an unnamed ספרא follows רבי יהודה. So the teaching from Step 6 is really his. That clashes with Step 2, which said the 'both die' ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed teaching in the ספרא, which follows רבי יהודה
Who is it? Whose opinion is this?

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources (Step 5 and Steps 6-7) show that רבי יהודה holds the eleventh animal is offered. So the 'both die' ברייתא cannot follow him.

phrases.english: An unattributed Sifra, whose is it? Rabbi Yehuda's,
and it teaches: "Of the herd"
comes to include the eleventh animal as a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the ספרא from Step 6 to רבי יהודה, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds the eleventh animal is offered, which undermines Step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that an unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The 'both die' ברייתא is about tithe in present times
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ברבי אבא explains before רבי יוחנן that the ברייתא saying both animals die is about מעשר nowadays. Since they cannot be offered, they are left to die out of concern for a תקלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון ברבי אבא explained it in front of רבי יוחנן: We are dealing with מעשר in present times, and they die because of the worry of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that the 'both die' ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It gives a new explanation for why the animals must die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש the animals cannot be sacrificed, and while they are alive people might misuse them, for example by shearing them or working with them. So 'they die' does not come from a rule about תמורה. It is a protective measure for our times, and that fits every opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he interpreted the ברייתא
In present times, when there is no בית המקדש
A mishap, meaning the risk that someone will misuse holy animals

steps.whatToRemember: The 'both die' ruling is not about the basic law of a mistaken מעשר. It is a special outcome for our times, because the animals cannot be offered and might be misused.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the death ruling through practical conditions rather than a dispute about תמורה. That removes the contradiction in רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Abba explained it
before Rabbi Yochanan:
We are dealing with tithe in the present time,
and [they die] because of concern for a mishap.
phrases.notes: For example, someone might shear them, work them, or eat them before they get a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 7 knocks down the רבי יהודה explanation, this gives a new way to explain the 'both die' ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ruling is limited to present-day מעשר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'both die' ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds a תמורת מעשר dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about מעשר nowadays. The animals die as a precaution against misuse, not because of the laws of תמורה.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention two animals?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason both animals die is that מעשר cannot be offered nowadays, then even one animal should have to die. So why does the ברייתא speak about two?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why mention specifically two? Even one animal would also have to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of רבי שמעון ברבי אבא from step 8. It asks why the ברייתא bothered to describe a case of two animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the animals die because nowadays there is no בית המקדש, so they cannot be offered and might cause a תקלה. That reason works just as well for a single animal. So the detail of 'two' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is correct)

phrases.english: If so, why specifically two?
phrases.notes: 'If so' refers to the explanation that this is about מעשר nowadays.

phrases.english: Even one also!
phrases.notes: A single tithe animal cannot be offered nowadays either.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא תְּרֵי? אֲפִילּוּ חַד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in light of the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice to describe two animals, given step 8's explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given (no offering nowadays) applies equally to one animal, so mentioning two seems pointless.

steps.title: Two animals teach a bigger point than one
steps.stepSummary: The תנא uses a 'not only this, but even that' style. With one animal the loss is small, so of course it dies. With two animals the loss is big, so we might have let them wait for a blemish and then eat them. The ברייתא teaches that even two must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary.' It is not necessary to say this about one animal, since there is no big loss. But with two, since the loss is great, I might think: let him keep them until they get a blemish and then eat them. So the ברייתא teaches us that they still must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It explains that 'two' is the bigger chiddush, not a limitation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing one animal is a small loss, so letting it die is obvious. Losing two is a bigger loss, so we might have allowed a gentler solution: wait for a blemish (a מום) and then eat it. The ברייתא picks the harder case to show that the rule holds even there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (a teaching style that states the harder case to include the easier one)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'two' as meaning that one animal is allowed. The case of two is mentioned because it is the harder case. One animal certainly must die too.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
phrases.notes: The תנא states the bigger case, and the smaller case is obvious.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא חַד דְּלֵית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא,
phrases.english: It is not necessary to say this about one, which has no big loss,
but with two, since the loss is great —

phrases.aramaic: לִישַׁהִינְהוּ עַד דְּנִיפּוֹל בְּהוּ מוּמָא וְלֵיכְלִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: I might think he should keep them until they get a blemish and then eat them,
phrases.notes: A blemished בכור or מעשר may be eaten outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that even two must die).

steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the harder case is stated so that the easier case is included
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two animals, the large loss would justify waiting for a blemish and eating them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even two animals must be left to die. Concern for a תקלה outweighs the financial loss.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא mentions two animals because that is the bigger loss. Even then, the animals are left to die nowadays and we do not wait for a blemish.

steps.title: An agent who calls the wrong animal 'tenth': רב פפי's view
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: someone sends an agent to tithe his animals. רב פפי in the name of רבא says that if the agent called the ninth 'tenth', it is holy. If he called the eleventh 'tenth', it is not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Someone says to his agent, 'Go and tithe for me.' רב פפי said in the name of רבא: If the agent called the ninth animal 'tenth', it is holy. If he called the eleventh 'tenth', it is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about a שליח (agent) who makes a counting mistake while tithing. It brings the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ninth is called 'tenth', it gets the holiness of מעשר. It may still be eaten after it gets a blemish, so the owner loses little and does not mind. When the eleventh is called 'tenth', it would become a שלמים, as discussed earlier. That is a bigger loss the owner would not accept, so the agent's act does not work.

phrases.english: It was stated: One who says to his agent, 'Go and tithe for me,'
Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
If he called the ninth 'tenth', it is holy,
phrases.notes: The owner does not mind, because it can still be eaten after a blemish.

phrases.english: but if he called the eleventh 'tenth', it is not holy.
phrases.notes: It would become a שלמים, a loss the owner would not accept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָאוֹמֵר לִשְׁלוּחוֹ צֵא וְעַשֵּׂר עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It builds on the earlier discussion that an eleventh animal called 'tenth' becomes a שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent's mistake with the ninth animal takes effect. A mistake with the eleventh does not, because the owner would not accept that bigger loss.

steps.title: רב פפא: The agent was sent to help, not to harm
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא disagrees. Even when the ninth is called 'tenth', it is not holy, because the owner can say: 'I sent you to benefit me, not to harm me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: Even if he called the ninth 'tenth', it is not holy. The owner can tell him: 'I sent you to fix things for me, not to ruin them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second, stricter opinion about the agent. In this view, any mistake by the agent fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that an agent's authority only covers acting properly for the owner. Any deviation that hurts the owner, even a small one like the ninth animal, is outside his job. So nothing he did takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: I sent you to fix (benefit) things

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea 'לתקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי' is a basic rule of שליחות across ש״ס. An agent who acts against the owner's interest is no longer acting as his agent.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
Even if he called the ninth 'tenth', it is not holy,
because he (the owner) can say to him:
'I sent you to fix things, not to ruin them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ קָרָא לַתְּשִׁיעִי עֲשִׂירִי אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפי's opinion in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent who deviates from proper tithing to the owner's harm accomplishes nothing, even in the ninth-animal case.

steps.title: Challenge from the agent who separates תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this differs from a משנה about תרומה. There, an agent who gives more or less than the owner's likely amount still makes valid תרומה. So why shouldn't the agent's mistake work here too?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned in a משנה: One who tells his agent 'Go and separate תרומה', the agent separates according to what the owner would want. If he does not know what the owner wants, he separates a middle amount, one out of fifty. If he went ten less or ten more (one out of forty or one out of sixty), his תרומה is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's rule that an agent who harms the owner accomplishes nothing. It does this with a משנה about separating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תרומה case, giving one out of forty instead of fifty takes away more of the owner's produce. That is a harm to the owner, yet the משנה says the תרומה counts. The owner could have said 'I sent you to benefit me, not to harm me,' but the משנה ignores that claim. So it seems to contradict רב פפא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Subtracted ten' means changing the number in 'one out of fifty' to 'one out of forty'. That makes the תרומה bigger. 'Added ten' makes it 'one out of sixty', which is smaller. The bigger amount is the one that costs the owner more.

phrases.english: And how is this different from what we learned in a mishna:
One who says to his agent, 'Go and separate terumah' —
he separates according to the owner's intention.
phrases.notes: A generous person gives 1/40, an average person 1/50, a stingy person 1/60.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת —
phrases.english: If he does not know the owner's intention —
he separates a middle amount, one out of fifty.
If he subtracted ten or added ten —
phrases.notes: Meaning one out of forty or one out of sixty.

phrases.english: his terumah is valid terumah?
phrases.notes: Even though this may harm the owner, it still works. That seems to contradict רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's reasoning in step 12 with a משנה about תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that an agent's harmful deviation does not take effect (לתקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תרומה case, an agent who departs from the owner's wishes in a way that costs him still makes valid תרומה. So a harmful deviation by an agent does not automatically cancel his act.

steps.title: Guessing the owner's generosity versus making a counting mistake
steps.stepSummary: With תרומה, an agent who gives more or less was estimating the owner's generosity, so his act is valid. With מעשר בהמה, mislabeling an animal is a plain error, and the owner can say he never sent the agent to make errors.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, with תרומה, some people give generously and some give sparingly. So the agent can say: 'This is how I judged you.' Here, with מעשר, it is a mistake. So the owner can say: 'You should not have made a mistake.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. It explains why the agent's act works for תרומה but not for מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תרומה there is no single correct amount. People really do give different amounts, so the agent's choice was a fair estimate of the owner and stays within his mission. In מעשר there is one correct animal, the tenth. Calling the ninth 'tenth' is not an estimate. It is an error, and an error is outside what the owner sent him to do. This supports רב פפא's view in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A good eye.' Giving generously, meaning a larger amount of תרומה.
'A bad eye.' Giving sparingly, meaning a smaller amount of תרומה.
'I estimated you.' I judged what kind of giver you are.

steps.whatToRemember: An agent may make a reasonable judgment call that the owner might have made himself, as in תרומה. But a plain mistake, as in מעשר, does not count, because 'I sent you to help me, not to harm me.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the agent in תרומה is being excused for making a mistake. The point is that giving more or less תרומה is not a mistake at all, because both amounts are normal ways people give.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for the laws of agency (שליחות). An agent's act binds the owner when it is a reasonable reading of what the owner wants. It does not bind him when it is a clear error.

phrases.english: They say: There (with תרומה),
since there are those who separate with a generous eye,
and there are those who separate with a stingy eye,
he (the agent) can say: 'This is how I estimated you.'
phrases.notes: The agent explains that he judged the owner to be a generous or a stingy giver.

phrases.english: Here (with מעשר) it is a mistake,
he (the owner) can say: 'You should not have made a mistake.'
phrases.notes: The owner rejects the agent's act because it was outside his mission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13 by separating the תרומה case from the מעשר case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: estimating an amount that has no fixed size, versus erring on a fixed, defined act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an agent's different amount of תרומה still counts, perhaps an agent's wrong count in מעשר should also count.
steps.terutzMaskana: In תרומה the agent made a legitimate estimate within his mission. In מעשר he made a mistake, which falls outside his mission, so the animal is not holy.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מעשר בהמה and מסכת בכורות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter of מעשר בהמה, together with the announcement that מסכת בכורות is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מעשר בהמה, and מסכת בכורות is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional closing line that ends the chapter and the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses our wish to come back and learn this material again. Here it also marks the end of all of מסכת בכורות, so no new chapter follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' The formula said at the end of a פרק.
The tithe of animals. This is also the name of the last פרק of the מסכת.

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת בכורות ends with a מחלוקת about an agent who makes a counting mistake in מעשר. רב פפי in the name of רבא says that if the agent called the ninth 'tenth', it is holy. רב פפא says that even then it is not holy, because the owner sent him to help, not to harm. The גמרא then explains why an agent's estimate in תרומה is different from a plain mistake.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'Animal Tithe,'
and Tractate Bekhorot is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the מסכת after the final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק מעשר בהמה and מסכת בכורות are complete.
